title: Which questions each word answers
source: My reading of each word’s definition: aisafety.info on doomers, Reid Hoffman’s summary of his four groups on X (2025), the 2022 e/acc newsletter post, Forbes and Wikipedia on decels, Vitalik Buterin’s “My techno-optimism” (2023) and MIRI’s page on the 2008 foom debate.
hint: Hover, tap or focus a mark to see what the word says

columns.label: Good or bad
columns.detail: Does the word say whether AI turns out well or badly for people?

columns.label: How much
columns.detail: Does it say how much AI will change the world?

columns.label: How fast
columns.detail: Does it say how quickly AI will become more capable?

columns.label: What to do
columns.detail: Does it say how fast to build AI, or how to govern it?

outcome.note: Catastrophe is the core of the word

scale.note: Extinction or a permanent loss of control is change on the largest scale

pace.note: Some arguments for doom involve a fast takeoff, but the word doesn’t require one

action.note: The word is about the outcome, not the policy

outcome.note: Thinks we’ll be worse off with AI

scale.note: Says nothing about how much AI changes, only that the change is for the worse

pace.note: Says nothing about how quickly AI improves

action.note: Hoffman’s short definition says nothing about policy

outcome.note: Skeptics can be worried about AI’s harms or simply unimpressed

scale.note: Expects AI to change the world less than its builders and its critics expect

pace.note: Usually expects slower progress than the forecasts, though not always

outcome.note: Expects a bright future, if the risks are managed

scale.note: A bright future implies big benefits, but the word doesn’t say how big

pace.note: Says nothing about how quickly AI improves

action.note: Push ahead and manage the risks along the way

outcome.note: Implies the benefits are worth any risk, without saying how things turn out

scale.note: Says nothing about how much AI changes

pace.note: Says how fast to build, not how fast AI will improve

action.note: Build as fast as possible, without weighing the risks

outcome.note: Treats faster technological growth as good

scale.note: Welcomes change on the largest scale

pace.note: Says how fast we should go, not how fast AI will improve

outcome.note: Says nothing about how AI turns out

scale.note: Says nothing about how much AI changes

pace.note: Says how fast we should go, not how fast AI will improve

action.note: Slow down: it’s the word e/acc supporters use for anyone who wants to

outcome.note: Optimistic about technology, with risks worth defending against

scale.note: Says nothing about how much AI changes

pace.note: Says nothing about how quickly AI improves

action.note: Speed up technology, especially the kinds that help people defend themselves and keep power spread out

outcome.note: A fast takeoff could go well or badly; the word doesn’t say

scale.note: A jump to superintelligence implies huge change

pace.note: Very fast: that’s the whole word

action.note: Says nothing about what to do
